>The Industrial Revolution and its consequences have been a disaster for the human race.

No. The overall living conditions for humans have increased. I am not talking about the average which is skewed up because a few are living in incredible luxury - but the median is also very high compared to pre-industrial revolution.

>they have destabilized society, have made life unfulfilling, have subjected human beings to indignities, have led to widespread psychological suffering

Yes, to some extent. Depression is, for example, one of the many maladies of modern society. Indignities have been around and will continue to be around and can't be quantitatively measured thus have no relevance to anyone seeking an accurate perspective. 

>have inflicted severe damage on the natural world.

Yes. This is sad - and I think it is the result of technological development that wasn't focused in the right direction (i.e. cleaner means of energy production and more sustainable food) - alas, this is fault in our global economic system - because it is divorced from actual physical resources; an utter abomination based on speculation. 

>The continued development of technology will worsen the situation,[...] subject human beings to greater indignities and inflict greater damage on the natural world

No. I believe there is an inflection point in terms of environmental impact. Does uncle Ted have any more arguments in this regard? (supporting the viewpoint that it will only get worse)

> it may lead to increased physical suffering even in "advanced" countries.

Perhaps. It all depends on whether the power of automated weapons surpasses that of the world's armies. If that happens before we're all digital beings, we're pretty much fucked."}]
